title: Trump: New York Times editor changes FBI's Russia story to cover for Trump
description_short: Trump: New York Times editor changes FBI's Russia story to cover for Trump
description_medium: FBI officials met New York Times reporter Eric Lichtblau in September 2016 while the paper was preparing a story about alleged links between the Trump Organization and a Russian bank. The bureau worried that publication could interfere with its investigation, bringing investigators and reporters covering the same subject into contact.
description_long: In September 2016, the FBI met with New York Times reporter Eric Lichtblau after learning the paper was preparing a story about alleged ties between the Trump Organization and a Russian bank. Officials were concerned that publication could interfere with the bureau’s investigation into those connections. The meeting brought a federal inquiry and the Times’ reporting on the same subject into direct contact.

title: Federal Workers Fired for Being Transgender or Supporting Trans Rights
description_short: Federal Workers Fired for Being Transgender or Supporting Trans Rights
description_medium: Associated Press reporting in 2025 said Yosemite ranger and biologist Shannon “SJ” Joslin was fired after helping hang a transgender Pride flag on El Capitan. The story also reported that some park visitors could face prosecution under tightened protest restrictions. Joslin’s case linked the flag display to disputes over expression and enforcement in national parks.
description_long: Associated Press reporting in 2025 described the firing of Shannon “SJ” Joslin, a Yosemite National Park ranger and biologist. Joslin had helped hang a transgender Pride flag on El Capitan in May 2025. The flag display drew demonstrations, while some park visitors faced concerns about possible prosecution under tightened protest restrictions. The case brought attention to expression in national parks and the enforcement of protest rules.

title: Donald Trump breaks the law asking Russia to find more Clinton emails
description_short: Donald Trump breaks the law asking Russia to find more Clinton emails
description_medium: During a July 27, 2016 campaign news conference, Donald Trump publicly urged Russia to find emails Hillary Clinton had deleted from her private server. He said, “Russia, if you’re listening, I hope you’re able to find the 30,000 emails that are missing.” The appeal was directed at a foreign government during the presidential campaign.
description_long: On July 27, 2016, Donald Trump spoke at a campaign news conference and directly addressed Russia, asking it to locate emails Hillary Clinton had deleted from her private server. He said, “Russia, if you’re listening, I hope you’re able to find the 30,000 emails that are missing.” Clinton was his opponent in the presidential race, and the request concerned obtaining information about her through a foreign government. The remark became a notable episode in debate over foreign involvement in U.S. elections.
